🇲🇽🛢️ PEMEX HITS 388,000 BARRELS/DAY — GASOLINE OUTPUT UP 12.7%

Pemex produced 388,100 barrels of gasoline per day in April, a 12.7% annual increase. The Tula refinery led the national system at 99,600 bpd — up 30% year-over-year. Dos Bocas contributed 71,600 bpd.

Diesel production surged even harder: up 32.3% to 260,000 barrels per day.

While US gas prices hit $4.54/gallon amid the Iran war, Mexico's refining expansion keeps domestic fuel stable. Energy sovereignty isn't a slogan — it's 388,000 barrels a day.

🇲🇽🏭 30,000 FREE SPOTS — MEXICO'S PUBLIC AI CENTER TRIPLES CAPACITY

Mexico's public AI training center just opened 30,000 spots for its second generation — triple the 10,000 in January's first cohort. Five months, fully online, completely free.

The curriculum spans AI, cybersecurity, cloud computing, data analysis, and 5G infrastructure, with job placement pipelines into NVIDIA, Google, Meta, Microsoft, Oracle, IBM, AWS, and Intel.

While the US guts public science funding, Mexico is building a free pipeline from zero tech background to employment at the world's biggest tech firms. Registration open through July 5.

🇲🇽🔥 341-124: CONGRESS APPROVES JUDICIAL REFORM + FOREIGN INTERFERENCE CLAUSE

Mexico's Chamber of Deputies voted 341-124 to postpone the second judicial election to June 2028 — and approved a new constitutional cause for election nullity: proven foreign interference.

PAN and PRI voted against. The reform also creates a Coordinating Commission to vet judicial candidates. The foreign interference clause arrives as Chihuahua's governor faces impeachment over unauthorized CIA agents operating in her state.

They wanted to interfere. Mexico just made it constitutionally nullifiable.

🇲🇽🌎 TMEC FORMAL TALKS BEGIN — MEXICO SETS THE TABLE

Mexico opened the first formal round of TMEC renegotiations today in Mexico City, with Economy Secretary Marcelo Ebrard leading the Mexican delegation against US Deputy Trade Rep Jeff Goettman and 60 American business leaders.

Ebrard didn't sugarcoat it — "the conversations are complex and difficult" — but held firm: Mexico opposes the auto tariffs, considers the steel levy unfounded, and pointed out the avocado tariff backfired, boosting Canadian exports to the US instead.

Three rounds mapped out: May 27-29 in Mexico City, June 16-17 in Washington, July 20 back in Mexico. The table is set on Mexican soil first.
